messages:
alex_cs: Heads-up: customer Globex reported their batch import aborted at 23:59:58 PST with 429s even though billing portal shows monthly refill at 00:00 PST. They lost a large part of the upload.
lee_support: Oof. Do we have a sample response from their client? websocket or http?
alex_cs: HTTP POSTs, highly parallel, client sent this snippet:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
date: Tue, 10 May 2026 07:59:59 GMT
x-tenant: globex-corp
x-credits-remaining: 0
x-billing-next-refill: 1716000000
content-type: application/json

{"error":"quota_exhausted","detail":"monthly credits used"}
```
jordan_eng: Interesting header x-billing-next-refill is server epoch for refill, matches 00:00 PST. UI shows +250k right after though.
maria_sre: Likely a cache-stale limiter window. Our per-node limiter keeps an in-memory token balance and consumes without synchronous reads for perf. Refill writes to DB + emits pubsub event to invalidate. If edge misses event, it stays at zero.
sam_devx: Did the client maintain keepalive connections? Long-lived HTTP/1.1 connections can stick to a single edge instance and miss a later cache update.
lee_support: Customer said their job used ~200 parallel connections held open across the upload for 90s.
alex_cs: They also attached server timing: first 429 at 23:59:58, UI balance 00:00:02 shows +250312, by 00:00:07 their next POST succeeded. They want to know why some requests failed for ~8s after refill.
maria_sre: That gap is consistent with missed pubsub delivery or slow sync interval (we have a 10s sync by default). If edge didn't get event, it will only refresh on periodic sync or connection restart.
jordan_eng: We should check pubsub ack latencies for that minute and any liveness issues on the invalidation service. Also confirm if refill wrote a 'force_invalidate' flag for large customers.
sam_devx: Short term: advise customer to retry failed chunks with exponential backoff and to reuse short-lived connections. For their bulk uploader we can recommend chunk-level retries and reconnect at the refill boundary.
lee_support: Can we offer immediate remediation? e.g., temporary one-off credit grant to cover failed portion + engineering ticket?
\illing_bot: Note: provisional 2000 token goodwill credit queued for globex-corp pending approval. ref: CASE-20260510-GLOBEX
alex_cs: Customer asked about prevention: can Redwood pre-warm caches before refill for heavy-tenants?
maria_sre: Yes — options: (1) pre-publish invalidation at T-10s, (2) reduce sync interval for high-throughput tenants, (3) allow edge to accept transient negative balance for up to N seconds post-refill while sync completes. All configurable.
jordan_eng: Proposed short-term infra tasks: add a refill 'push' endpoint that writes to a control channel; instrument missed-event rates; add metrics for per-tenant cache staleness.
sam_devx: I'll prototype an internal balance-read endpoint that bypasses cache so support can validate DB vs local cache quickly: GET /internal/tenants/{id}/balance.
lee_support: Draft for customer response: apologize, explain refill occurred at 00:00 PST but some runtime instances briefly served stale zero balances causing 429s for in-flight requests. Offer compensatory credit and recommend client retries + reconnects.
alex_cs: Customer accepted the credit and asked for a follow-up engineering plan. Please file a post-incident ticket with timeline and proposed fixes.
maria_sre: Adding action items: 1) check pubsub delivery between 07:59:58-08:00:10 UTC; 2) lower sync interval for tier-enterprise tenants or implement pre-warm; 3) add cache-invalidate push on refill.
sam_devx: I'll open a PR for the internal balance route this sprint.
lee_support: Marking thread pending infra follow-up. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
